title: Coconut Grove in Marrero
summary: Foster's group left St. Charles Avenue for the Coconut Grove in Marrero run by the Seymour brothers, staying five years.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I heard you out there then about 1944 or so, once Austin Young told me he was working out there. You know, you were there with me. Yeah, I remember your name was on the sign too. I remember the name.

Yeah, that's where the boy was there. And, um, we left that giant, that club, and went to the Coconut Grove in Marrero. We stayed there five years. Oh, yeah. Over there. That's not what I told you about then. That was my group, see. We stayed there five years and made that man, that's the Seymour brothers. They're still over there right now. We've had the Coconut Grove, and they closed out. We stayed there five years. Where is that Coconut Grove?
I can't remember. In Marrero. Is it up past the Moulin Rouge, up the river? Up past the Moulin Rouge.
Up towards the bridge. Up past I would say about, oh, maybe a half mile. I've seen it.
I've never been in there. I don't blame. Oh, yes.
But would you play, I was playing the Marrero's at Fajro? Would you play in the Coconut Grove? Yeah. I went to Marrero's right after Kid Thomas.
Well, it was at the Grove, yeah.

That's right. That's right. Yeah, Fajro was. That's right, Fajro. That's right. That's the Marrero's. Right. When we played the Coconut Grove, we didn't open it up, but we went there to Hilgert and Boyce, you know. And this Junior Seymour, he came to the Avenue Lawrence, you know. Put a bunch of guys in the band and he told his brother and he had a place over in Marrero who would like for us to come over and play for him. He'd take a life to the band, you know. And then the next day he was over here and seeing me, you know. And we get the lady, we played there two more weeks and everybody noticed and went and played with them over there. And stayed at that place five years. And then he closed it out. Left there, in fact she made the Hummock, left there he opened the keyhole. We were doing some good business there, you know. The place was kind of small, but it was big enough to hold people, you know.
Keyhole is a new, that's a brother. That's a, that's a, I would call that West Vigo. West Vigo. After, after Marrero is a big one, isn't it? Yes, I think so.
